title: Thunder's leadership book (coordinated by Cris Pop), The Inner Fire: ownership is a decision, not passion
summary: The chapter argues that true inner fire is the quiet flame of responsibility, not magnetic passion: a decision to own outcomes regardless of motivation. Andreea Popa describes going first, quiet care, claiming what is "mine to take care of", trusting people, and owning your shadows. It reports that Cris told the team in a growth meeting they were "waiting to be told what to do", sparking a shift to ownership, illustrated by Cosmin's story.

principles.text: Real inner fire is the quiet flame of responsibility, a decision to own outcomes, not a passion that burns out.
principles.quote: True inner fire is the quiet flame of responsibility. It’s showing up consistently when you least want to, owning outcomes, and carrying weight others won’t bear.

principles.text: Go first: be vulnerable and admit mistakes so others feel safe to try, without waiting for certainty or readiness.
principles.quote: None of us has the right answer when we go first. That’s because going first should not be about certainty but about lighting the path so others feel brave enough to follow.

principles.text: Modern leadership is quiet care: take responsibility for mistakes and ask what would make work easier for people.
principles.quote: Who say, That’s my mistake, even when it’s not technically theirs, because taking responsibility moves things forward, and pointing fingers just keeps us stuck.

principles.text: Ownership grows when someone claims what nobody else wants; shared ownership by everyone means care by no one.
principles.quote: When everything belongs to nobody, nothing gets cared for.

principles.text: Trust people before results; being trusted turns executors into owners who build with you.
principles.quote: It happens the moment someone says I trust you and you realize, maybe for the first time, Oh, I’m not working for them—I’m building with them.

principles.text: Cris named the team's problem: waiting for permission and defaulting to leaders for decisions they should make themselves.
principles.quote: We’re not owning our work. We’re just waiting to be told what to do.
